title: Steering x Context-Length: Does a Steering Vector Decay Over Long Generations and Re-open Jailbreaks?

original_idea.body: Test whether a safety steering vector's effect decays over long generations exactly where many-shot/long-context jailbreaks strengthen.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete medium-horizon long-context jailbreak threat; chain from steering decay to re-opened jailbreaks is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Long-generation inference with position-resolved measurement is guided but adds memory/engineering; mentor-supported.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single focused experiment: harmful-compliance vs generation position/context length, steered vs unsteered.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public jailbreak prompts, no internal access; long-context defense decay is externally valuable.

low_compute.reasoning: Long-context generation raises memory/compute; single mid GPU days, heavier than short-context.

novelty.reasoning: The temporal-decay-of-steering meets-long-context interaction appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Steering effect decaying over long generations aligning with long-context jailbreaks is an underexplored interaction.
